Sampled there, the button fill is #ee325d with #ffffff text, 4.00:1. The live server HTML gives this button's CSS directly: background-color #EE325D, color #FFFFFF, font-weight 500, font-size 0.875rem overridden to 1rem, so 14-16px, not large text, and 4.5:1 applies. The 'axe-core could not decide' clause is about Rampa's process and cannot be checked, but the colours and ratio it reports hold in the capture and in the live CSS. I found no contrast switch in the Perto Digital plugin that could satisfy G174, and no exception applies. captureDiffers: no, the live CSS matches the captured colours. The element fails 1.4.3 for the reason the claim names.

Reasons I looked for that would make it pass and did not find: the page carries a Perto Digital accessibility plugin, but the capture lists only voice assistant, Libras and face navigation, no contrast switch that would satisfy G174; the pink is not a hover or focus state but the resting style (every card button on the page has it). captureDiffers: the cards are rendered client-side, so the live server HTML I fetched does not hold them, but its __NEXT_DATA__ lists the same courses in the same order and its theme sets the action colour to #EE325D, and the header CTA's live CSS is background #EE325D with color #FFFFFF; the screenshot is a fully styled Chromium render, so nothing suggests users get other colours. The element fails 1.4.3 for the reason the claim gives.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the course search combobox under the 'Graduação' banner; its only label is the placeholder 'Pesquisar' (accessible name from placeholder, no visible label). In the screenshot the placeholder glyphs reach #767676 on a #f5f5f5 field, 4.17:1, which is #121212 at alpha 0x8f composited on #f5f5f5, as the message says. At 16px weight 500 it is not large text, so 4.5:1 applies. Reasons it could pass that I checked: 1.4.3's exceptions (inactive component, decoration, logotype) do not cover placeholder text in an active field, and the W3C WAI forms tutorial treats browser-default placeholder colours as not meeting WCAG's minimum contrast and shows how to style them to meet it, so placeholder text is text under 1.4.3; no contrast switch was found in the accessibility plugin. captureDiffers: the search field is rendered client-side and is absent from the live server HTML, so I could only compare the theme (same palette) and the styled Chromium render; nothing suggests a different placeholder colour for users. The element fails 1.4.3 for the reason the claim names.
